examples.en: My uncle went on a business trip for official duties.

examples.ko: 공무 중인 경찰관을 방해하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You must not obstruct a police officer on duty.

examples.ko: 공무를 맡은 사람은 더 책임감이 있어야 해요.
examples.en: People in public service should have a stronger sense of responsibility.

examples.ko: 공무 때문에 오늘 모임에 못 가요.
examples.en: I can't go to today's meeting because of official business.

examples.ko: 그는 공무를 마치고 바로 집으로 돌아왔어요.
examples.en: He came straight home after finishing his official duties.

examples.ko: 공무 차량은 주차 구역이 따로 있어요.
examples.en: Government vehicles have separate parking zones.

explain: 국가나 공공 기관에서 하는 일을 말해요. 회사 일은 '업무', 개인적인 일은 '사적인 일'이라고 해서 구분해요. '공무원'과 '공무 수행' 같은 말로 자주 만나요.
explain_en: It means work done for the state or a public institution. Company work is 업무 and personal matters are 사적인 일, so the three are kept apart. You often meet it in 공무원 and 공무 수행.

examples.ko: 그 일은 제 밥줄이라서 포기할 수 없어요.
examples.en: That job is my livelihood, so I can't give it up.
If the company closes down, my livelihood will be in danger.

examples.ko: 밥줄을 쥐고 있는 사람에게 누가 대들겠어요?
examples.en: Who would dare to challenge the person who holds your livelihood in their hands?

examples.ko: 이 업계는 밥줄이 걸린 문제라 모두 예민해요.
examples.en: In this industry, livelihoods are at stake, so everyone is sensitive.

examples.ko: 아버지는 평생 이 가게를 밥줄 삼아 사셨어요.
examples.en: My father lived his whole life relying on this shop for his livelihood.

examples.ko: 괜히 말했다가 밥줄이 날아갈까 봐 걱정이에요.
examples.en: I'm worried I might lose my job if I speak up for nothing.

explain: 먹고사는 수단, 곧 일자리를 비유적으로 말해요. '밥줄이 끊기다', '밥줄을 쥐다'처럼 짝으로 많이 써요. 조금 거친 구어 느낌이라 격식 있는 글에서는 '생계'라고 해요.
explain_en: It figuratively refers to the means by which you earn your food, that is, your job. It often pairs as '밥줄이 끊기다' and '밥줄을 쥐다'. It feels a bit blunt and colloquial, so formal writing uses '생계' instead.

examples.en: On bok days, we go out to eat samgyetang.

examples.ko: 올해 첫 복날은 날씨가 정말 더웠어요.
examples.en: The first bok day this year was really hot.
When bok day comes, the line is long at every restaurant.
On bok day evening, I ate chicken soup with my family.

examples.ko: 복날을 앞두고 시장에서 닭 값이 올랐어요.
examples.en: Chicken prices went up at the market ahead of bok day.
The bok-day kind of heat is still going on.

explain: 초복, 중복, 말복처럼 여름에 가장 더운 때의 날들을 부르는 말이에요. 이날에는 삼계탕 같은 음식을 먹으며 몸을 챙기는 풍습이 있어요. 날씨 뉴스에서 '복날 더위'라고도 해요.
explain_en: It is a general name for the hottest summer days, namely 초복, 중복 and 말복. People have a custom of eating dishes like samgyetang on these days to take care of their health. Weather news also uses the phrase '복날 더위'.

examples.en: The puppy wagging its tail looks so endearing.

examples.ko: 그 아이는 말투가 애교스러워서 인기가 많아요.
examples.en: That child is popular because of the charming way he talks.
It's hard to refuse when someone asks in a cute, charming voice.
My younger sibling charmingly asked for some pocket money.
The cat rubbed against my leg in an endearing way.

examples.ko: 애교스럽지 않은 성격이라 이런 건 어색해요.
examples.en: I'm not the charming type, so this feels awkward.

explain: '귀엽다'는 겉모습에도 쓰지만, '애교스럽다'는 상냥하고 사랑스러운 말투나 행동에 더 많이 써요. 사람과 동물 모두에게 쓰고, '애교를 부리다'와 함께 알아 두면 좋아요. ㅂ 불규칙이라 '애교스러워요', '애교스러운'으로 바뀌어요.
explain_en: '귀엽다' can describe looks too, but '애교스럽다' is used more for sweet, lovable speech and behavior. It applies to both people and animals, and it pairs well with '애교를 부리다'. It is a ㅂ-irregular adjective, so it becomes '애교스러워요' and '애교스러운'.

examples.en: Our youngest is a spoiled baby.

examples.ko: 응석꾸러기 동생이 또 안아 달라고 해요.
examples.en: My clingy little sibling is asking to be held again.
Even though he's grown up, he acts like a spoiled child.
I was a spoiled child when I was little.
I try not to raise him to be spoiled.
That puppy is such a clingy little one.

explain: '-꾸러기'는 '장난꾸러기', '잠꾸러기'처럼 그런 버릇이 많은 사람을 가리켜요. 아이한테는 귀엽게 말할 수 있지만, 어른에게 쓰면 놀리는 느낌이 있어요. 강아지 같은 동물에게도 써요.
explain_en: The ending '-꾸러기' points to someone with a lot of a certain habit, as in '장난꾸러기' (prankster) or '잠꾸러기' (sleepyhead). It can sound cute for a child, but for an adult it feels teasing. It is also used for animals such as puppies.

en: retake the college entrance exam after a year of study

examples.en: I failed to get into college, so I am preparing a second time.
My friend spent a year preparing to retake the exam.
While retaking the exam year, I went to a cram school.
I am still deciding whether to retake the exam.
After the extra year, I got into the major I wanted.
This time I will study another year and definitely pass.

explain: 대학 입시에 떨어지거나 만족하지 못해서 한 해 더 준비하는 일에 쓰고, 두 번째 도전은 '재수', 세 번째는 '삼수'라고 해요. 일반 시험이나 자격증에는 쓰지 않고 '다시 도전하다'라고 해요. '재수 없다'의 '재수'(운)와 소리만 같고 다른 말이에요.
explain_en: It is for spending another year preparing after failing or being unhappy with the college entrance exam; the second try is '재수' and the third is '삼수'. For other exams or certificates, say '다시 도전하다'. It only sounds like the '재수' (luck) in '재수 없다'; it is a different word.
